contentEn:
BC has no provincial law setting a maximum renovation deposit. That blank space is where homeowners get hurt. Reno Stars has written hundreds of contracts across Vancouver, Richmond, and Burnaby — here is what BC homeowners actually need to know in 2026.

How Much Deposit Is Normal for a BC Renovation?

BC sets no ceiling on deposits, but the market has established norms. For projects under $10,000, expect 10–20 percent. For larger whole-home renovations from $50,000–$150,000, 5–10 percent is standard. Any contractor asking for 30–50 percent upfront is shifting all completion risk onto you — that is a warning sign worth heeding.

Deposits and progress payments are not the same. A deposit is paid before work begins. A progress payment is paid as defined stages are completed. Confusing the two leads to paying for work that has not started.

What Your Contract Must Say About the Deposit

A proper BC renovation contract must specify: the exact deposit amount, what it covers, refund conditions, and consequences if either party walks away. Without those terms in writing, your deposit is effectively a gift. The contract should also list every project milestone and tie a payment to each one.

BC's Home Improvement Contracts regulation (under the Business Practices and Investments Act) gives homeowners a 10-day cooling-off period. For contracts negotiated at your door or through door-to-door sales, you may cancel within 10 days and receive your full deposit back. This right does not apply to contracts signed in a showroom or through competitive tender.

Red Flags in Renovation Deposits

BC Consumer Protection BC issued warnings in 2023 about several Metro Vancouver contractors who collected large deposits and then closed before starting work. Homeowner losses ranged from $15,000 to over $80,000. The warning signs are consistent:

  • Asking for more than 20–30 percent upfront
  • Insisting on cash or Interac with no written record
  • Pressuring you to waive the cooling-off period
  • Asking you to pay suppliers directly for materials — this breaks the contractor's accountability for delivery and quality

A Safe Payment Schedule by Milestone

A milestone-based payment structure protects both parties. For a typical larger renovation:

  • 10% on signing — secures your place in the schedule
  • 15–25% when materials are delivered to site
  • 25–35% when rough-in passes inspection
  • 20–30% when practical completion is reached
  • 10% on final handover

For a $75,000 kitchen and bathroom renovation, a safe deposit is $7,500–$11,250 (10–15%). The next milestone payment triggers after cabinets and countertops are confirmed and on site.

Change Orders: How to Handle Mid-Project Costs

Most renovations encounter scope changes. A signed written change order — signed by both you and your contractor before new work begins — is the only thing that makes an extra charge legitimate. Never pay for an addition without a signed change order. Verbal agreements are not legally enforceable in BC renovation disputes.

contentZh:
卑詩省對裝修定金沒有省級法律設定上限。這個法律空白正是業主容易受損的地方。Reno Stars在溫哥華、列治文和本拿比簽訂了數百份合同——以下是你在2026年真正需要了解的。

卑詩省裝修定金正常是多少？

卑詩省對定金沒有最高限額，但市場已形成行業規範。對於1萬元以下的項目，定金通常為10％至20％。對於5萬至15萬元的全屋裝修項目，定金標準為5％至10％。任何要求預付30％至50％定金的公司，都在將所有工程完成風險轉嫁給業主——這是一個值得警惕的危險信號。

定金和進度款不是同一回事。定金是工程開始前支付的錢；進度款則是按定義好的工程階段完成後再支付的費用。將兩者混淆會導致您為尚未開始的工程付款。

合同中應如何約定定金條款

規範的卑詩省裝修合同必須列明：具體定金金額、涵蓋範圍、退款條件以及任何一方退出的後果。沒有這些書面條款，您的定金實際上是一筆贈款。合同還應列出每個項目里程碑，並將每筆付款與相應里程碑掛鉤。

卑詩省的《家庭裝修合同》條例給予業主10天冷靜期。對於上門推銷或街邊銷售談判簽訂的合同，您可在10天內取消並全額退還定金。該權利不適用於在陳列室簽署的合同或通過競爭性招標簽訂的合同。

裝修定金的危險信號

2023年，卑詩省消費者保護局針對大溫哥華地區多家裝修公司發出警示——這些公司在收取大選定金後，在工程開工前就已停業。涉及的業主損失從$15,000元到$80,000元以上不等。危險信號始終一致：要求預付超過20–30％，堅持收取現金且無書面記錄，以及施壓要求放棄冷靜期。

還要注意那些將材料費單獨列出、要求業主直接向供應商付款的公司。這種做法切斷了裝修公司對材料交付和質量的問責。

安全的里程碑付款結構

對於典型大型裝修項目：簽署合同時支付10％，材料到場交付時支付15–25％，隱蔽工程通過驗收時支付25–35％，實用工程完成時支付20–30％，最後10％在移交日結清。

以一個$75,000元的廚房和衛生間裝修為例，安全定金範圍為$7,500至$11,250元（10–15％）。

變更單：如何處理施工中途增項

大多數裝修項目都會遇到範圍變更。在新工程開始前，由雙方簽署的書面變更單，是使額外收費具有合法性的唯一憑據。在沒有任何憑據的情況下，永遠不要為增項付款。口頭約定的額外費用在卑詩省裝修糾紛中不具備法律強制執行力。
